title: Distances to Japan use different reference points and units
reading: Use the geographic fixes, not a distance ring
basis: Doolittle’s navigator coordinate is about 1,231 km from the Tokyo district used here. It does not exactly reproduce either prose distance; coast versus city and nautical versus statute miles matter.

records.says: Gives the launch as approximately 824 statute miles east of central Tokyo.
Describes the first launch as approximately 650 miles from Tokyo.

title: When the picket was sighted
basis: Use Hornet’s first sighting; the ships had different viewpoints.

records.says: Patrol craft sighted at 0738, bearing 220°, 20,000 yards.
Patrol vessel sighted at 0744, bearing 221°, 10,000 yards.
Identifies the sighting vessel as No. 23 Nittō Maru.

title: Doolittle’s launch time
basis: The pilot and Enterprise agree; retain Hornet’s five-minute difference.

records.says: Take off at 8:20 A.M. ship time.
First B-25 launched at 0825.
First bomber launched at 0820.

title: The offshore launch position
reading: Hornet’s 0800 fix, followed by a reconstructed 22-knot turn into wind
basis: The latitude difference is about 31 km; use a 40 km horizontal bound. Neither point is an exact deck trajectory.

records.says: Navigator gives take-off at 35°43′N, 153°25′E.

title: Farrow leaves last
basis: Use the individual aircraft account; naval completion reports differ by one or two minutes.

records.says: Farrow’s 40-2268 took off at 9:19 a.m. ship time.
Last bomber launched at 0920.
Last bomber off at 0921.

title: Reported hits and the raid’s material effect
reading: Local destruction and civilian deaths; limited overall military damage
basis: Aircrew claims are not a surveyed damage assessment. No destroyed target or confirmed fighter-kill symbols are drawn.

records.says: Initial assessment claimed damage exceeded expectations.
Pilot observations describe explosions and fires, including residential districts.
Postwar count: 87 killed, 151 seriously injured and more than 311 lightly injured in Japan.

title: What Greening bombed
reading: A broad district east of Tokyo, with 40 km uncertainty
basis: The identification is a crew report; no exact refinery footprint is asserted. This uncertainty also covers the route to it.

records.says: Reported an oil refinery and storage tanks.
Identifies a reported refinery near Sakura; Yokohama primary not reached.

title: Watson’s target identification
reading: Tokyo industrial district, not an identified building
basis: The summary itself records competing identifications. Use a 40 km bound.

records.says: Tokyo Gas and Electric; the same target was also reported as a tank and truck factory.

basis: An editorial placement within the raid, constrained by the launch, destination and feasible transit. The route and minute are reconstructed; this does not establish a bomb impact location.

title: Doolittle’s crew abandons its bomber
basis: Use the pilot’s time at the end of the navigator’s five-minute interval; no second-level accuracy is claimed.

records.says: Pilot gives 21:20 ship time.
Navigator gives 21:15–21:20.

title: Confused early reports of Hallmark’s fate
basis: Use the later coastal account; do not map the unconfirmed Poyang report as a crash site.

records.says: Initial information placed Hallmark near Nanchang/Poyang and explicitly warned it was unreliable.
Crew 6 ditched; three captured.
Hallmark’s bomber ditched off Wenzhou. Dieter and Fitzmaurice drowned.

title: Confused early reports of Farrow’s fate
basis: This is a recovery region, not a precise bailout or capture coordinate.

records.says: Places Farrow near Shipu and warns that accounts of his and Hallmark’s crews may be confused.
All five of Farrow’s crew became prisoners.

title: Why the intended landing was not available
reading: Weather, fuel, disrupted timing and incomplete coordination
basis: The immediate crew experience and the official planning history explain different parts of the failure; do not blame it solely on weather or portray Chinese assistance as absent.

records.says: Could not raise Chuchow by radio; cloud and darkness prevented a landing.
Secrecy restricted Chinese information; fields expected arrivals later, and Chiang resisted using Chuchow.

title: Deaths in the Zhejiang–Jiangxi campaign
reading: An estimated 250,000, with the total uncertain
basis: This describes the subsequent 1942 campaign, not deaths on 18 April or a count of people who directly helped airmen. No raid-day timestamp is assigned.

records.says: Estimates a quarter-million deaths; documents massacres, destruction and biological warfare.
Attributes 250,000 to Chiang Kai-shek and Chennault; says the real total is unknown.
